table.name: account
table.purpose: Bank accounts table (PKDD'99 Czech financial dataset): one row per bank account, recording its opening date, the district where it was opened, and how often statements are issued. Accounts link to clients via disp, and to loans, orders, and transactions.

account_id.name: account_id
account_id.description: Unique identifier of the bank account; primary key of this table. Referenced by loan, disp, trans, and order tables.

date.name: account_opened_date
date.description: Date the account was opened (creation date), ranging from 1993-01-01 to 1997-12-29.

district_id.name: district_id
district_id.description: Foreign key to the district table identifying the district (region) where the account was opened; values 1-77 correspond to Czech districts (e.g. 35 = Jablonec n. Nisou, 77 = Vsetin).

frequency.name: statement_frequency
frequency.description: Statement issuance frequency, in Czech: 'POPLATEK MESICNE' = monthly statement issuance, 'POPLATEK TYDNE' = weekly, 'POPLATEK PO OBRATU' = after each transaction. (Literal translation 'fee monthly/weekly/after turnover'; in the source PKDD'99 Czech bank dataset this field is the statement frequency.)

table.name: card
table.purpose: One row per bank payment card issued to a client disposition (disp), recording the card type and issue date. Links cards to clients/accounts via the disposition table. This matches the classic PKDD'99 Czech bank financial dataset 'card' table.

card_id.name: card_id
card_id.description: Primary key of the card table; unique identifier for each issued payment card.

disp_id.name: disp_id
disp_id.description: Foreign key to disp.disp_id, identifying the client disposition (the person's role on an account) to which the card was issued. One-to-one: each card belongs to exactly one disposition.

issued.name: issued
issued.description: Date the card was issued (stored as text, e.g. 'YYYY-MM-DD'), ranging from 1993-11-07 to 1998-12-29.

table.name: client
table.purpose: One row per bank client (customer) — a person, identified by client_id, with birth date, gender, and home district. Clients are linked to accounts via the disp (disposition) table. This matches the classic PKDD'99 Czech bank (Berka) financial dataset schema.

birth_date.name: birth_date
birth_date.description: Client's date of birth (ISO date). Range 1911–1987 is consistent with birth dates of bank customers; no evidence of another interpretation.

client_id.name: client_id
client_id.description: Unique surrogate identifier of the client; primary key of the client table. Referenced one-to-one by disp.client_id (the disposition linking clients to accounts).

district_id.name: district_id
district_id.description: Foreign key to district.district_id — the region/district where the client lives (many-to-one; lookup labels are Czech district names such as Jablonec n. Nisou, Vyskov, Vsetin).

table.name: disp
table.purpose: Disposition table: links clients to bank accounts, specifying each client's role on the account (owner or authorized disponent/user). It is the join entity between client and account, and the anchor through which cards are issued (card.disp_id). One row per client-account relationship (5369 rows: 4500 owners for 4500 accounts plus 869 authorized users).

account_id.name: account_id
account_id.description: Identifier of the bank account this disposition links the client to. References account.account_id; an account can have multiple dispositions (one OWNER plus possibly DISPONENT users).

client_id.name: client_id
client_id.description: Identifier of the client (person) attached to the account. One-to-one with disp_id here, but in general a client could be linked to accounts; references client.client_id.

disp_id.name: disp_id
disp_id.description: Primary key of the disposition record (the client-account relationship). Referenced by card.disp_id, i.e. a payment card is issued through a disposition.

type.name: type
type.description: Type of the client's relationship to the account: 'OWNER' (account holder, exactly one per account, 4500 rows) or 'DISPONENT' (authorized additional user, 869 rows).

table.name: district
table.purpose: Demographic and socioeconomic profile of the 77 Czech districts (name, region, population, municipality-size breakdown, urbanization, average salary, unemployment, entrepreneurship, and crime counts for 1995/1996). Referenced by clients and accounts to provide regional context for banking data.

A10.name: urban_inhabitant_ratio
A10.description: Ratio of urban inhabitants (%), 33.9–100.0; Prague reaches 100.0.

A11.name: average_salary
A11.description: Average (unemployment-relevant) salary in the district, in CZK; values 8110–12541, mean ~9032.

A13.name: unemployment_rate_1996
A13.description: Unemployment rate in 1996 (%), 0.43–9.4; slightly higher than the 1995 rate in most districts.

A15.name: crimes_1995
A15.description: Number of committed crimes in 1995; 818–85677 (Prague is the extreme outlier).

A16.name: crimes_1996
A16.description: Number of committed crimes in 1996; 888–99107 (Prague outlier).

A2.name: district_name
A2.description: District name (Czech administrative district, e.g. 'Benesov', 'Brno - mesto'); unique per row.

A3.name: region
A3.description: Region of the Czech Republic the district belongs to (8 values: Prague, central/north/south/east Bohemia, north/south Moravia).

A4.name: inhabitants
A4.description: Number of inhabitants of the district (stored as text); 42,821–1,204,953 (Prague).

A5.name: municipalities_lt_500
A5.description: Number of municipalities with fewer than 500 inhabitants (stored as text).

A6.name: municipalities_500_1999
A6.description: Number of municipalities with 500–1,999 inhabitants (stored as text).

A7.name: municipalities_2000_9999
A7.description: Number of municipalities with 2,000–9,999 inhabitants (stored as text).

A8.name: municipalities_ge_10000
A8.description: Number of municipalities with 10,000 or more inhabitants (stored as text); 0–5.

A9.name: number_of_cities
A9.description: Number of cities in the district, 1–11.

district_id.name: district_id
district_id.description: Primary key: identifier of the district (1–77), referenced by account.district_id and client.district_id.

table.name: loan
table.purpose: One row per loan granted to a bank account: principal, term, monthly payment, grant date, and repayment status. Each account has at most one loan (one-to-one with account).

account_id.name: account_id
account_id.description: Identifier of the account that took out the loan. Joins one-to-one to account.account_id (each account has at most one loan in this table).

amount.name: amount
amount.description: Principal of the loan, in the account's currency (Czech koruna in the source banking dataset). Ranges from 4,980 to 590,820.

date.name: date
date.description: Date the loan was granted, between 1993-07-05 and 1998-12-08.

duration.name: duration
duration.description: Loan term in months; only the values 12, 24, 36, 48, 60 occur.

loan_id.name: loan_id
loan_id.description: Unique identifier of the loan; primary key of this table.

payments.name: payments
payments.description: Fixed monthly installment for the loan (amount / duration rounded), in the same currency as amount. Ranges from 304 to 9,910.

status.name: status
status.description: Loan repayment status code: A = contract finished, loan paid off; B = contract finished, loan not paid (defaulted); C = contract running, payments OK; D = contract running, client in debt/arrears. (This matches the standard PKDD'99 financial dataset coding; the values alone support 'finished vs running' and 'good vs bad' groupings but the exact letter meanings are inferred from that known schema.)

table.name: order
table.purpose: Standing (permanent) payment orders: recurring payments set up on a bank account, each transferring a fixed amount to a beneficiary account at a given bank, characterized by a payment type (k_symbol). One row per order; an account may have several orders. This matches the 'orders' table of the PKDD'99 Czech financial dataset.

account_id.name: account_id
account_id.description: Identifier of the account that issues the payment order (the debited account). Foreign key to account.account_id; an account can have multiple standing orders.

account_to.name: account_to
account_to.description: Account number of the beneficiary (the account to which the payment is sent). Not a foreign key within this database — it refers to accounts at external banks, hence the large, near-unique values.

amount.name: amount
amount.description: Amount of the recurring payment, in the account's currency (CZK in the source bank data). Range 1–14,882, median ~2,596.

bank_to.name: bank_to
bank_to.description: Code of the beneficiary's bank (two-letter anonymized bank code). 13 distinct codes; pairs with account_to to identify the destination account.

k_symbol.name: k_symbol
k_symbol.description: Characterization of the payment purpose (Czech abbreviations): SIPO = household/utility payments, POJISTNE = insurance premium, UVER = loan repayment, LEASING = leasing payment, empty = unspecified/other.

order_id.name: order_id
order_id.description: Primary key; unique identifier of the payment order (standing order).

table.name: trans
table.purpose: Bank account transaction ledger: one row per transaction on an account, with date, type/operation, amount, resulting balance, and for transfers the counterparty bank and account number. This matches the PKDD'99 Czech bank 'trans' table (Czech labels: VYDAJ=expense, PRIJEM=income, VYBER=withdrawal, VKLAD=deposit, PREVOD=transfer, UROK=interest, SIPO=household payment, SLUZBY=services, DUCHOD=pension, POJISTNE=insurance, UVER=loan).

account.name: counterparty_account_number
account.description: Counterparty account number for bank transfers (PREVOD NA UCET / PREVOD Z UCTU rows); null for cash and card transactions. The frequent value 0 likely means 'unknown/not applicable'. Not a foreign key to account.account_id (values are large synthetic account numbers, not the 1-11382 ids).

account_id.name: account_id
account_id.description: Identifier of the account on which the transaction was made; references account.account_id (many-to-one).

amount.name: amount
amount.description: Transaction amount in Czech koruna (CZK). Top value 15 (recurring household payment) and 0 (interest-related zero entries) are common.

balance.name: balance_after_transaction
balance.description: Account balance in CZK after the transaction; can be negative (overdraft, min -41126).

bank.name: counterparty_bank_code
bank.description: Code of the counterparty bank for transfers (two-letter codes, e.g. QR, AB, ST); null for non-transfer transactions.

k_symbol.name: transaction_characterization
k_symbol.description: Czech transaction characterization code: UROK = interest credited, SANKC. UROK = sanction interest (negative), SLUZBY = payment for services, SIPO = household payment, DUCHOD = old-age pension, POJISTNE = insurance payment, UVER = loan payment, SANKC. UROK = sanction interest for negative balance; blank/null = no characterization.

operation.name: operation
operation.description: Operation mode in Czech: VYBER = withdrawal in cash, VYBER KARTOU = credit card withdrawal, VKLAD = cash deposit, PREVOD Z UCTU = collection from another account, PREVOD NA UCET = transfer to another account. Null (17%) for rows where only 'type' is given (e.g. interest credit).

type.name: transaction_type
type.description: Transaction type in Czech: PRIJEM = credit (deposit/income), VYDAJ = debit (withdrawal/expense), VYBER = cash withdrawal (recorded separately from VYDAJ).
